title: feat(app-shell): Access pillar — permission-set header, five tabs (Objects · System capabilities · Row-level security · Tab visibility · Delegated admin), matrix restyle (objectui#12456)
body:
Fixes #12456
Clause-②: no

Studio's Access pillar shows an open permission set as an item header and five tabs (epic objectui#12446, decision C, ruled 2026-10-15), and the object matrix takes the artboard's look.

## Premise re-check (ruling C)

On `c950345` the Access content column still rendered the five sections as one stacked column. `PermissionMatrixEditPage` stacked System Capabilities, the filter bar, the legend and the object matrix. `PermissionAdvancedFacets` then stacked three collapsibles under it: Row-Level Security, Tab Visibility and Delegated Admin Scope. The premise holds, so the tabs are built as ruled.

## What changed

- **Item header (card target 2).** For an open set, `PermissionMatrixEditPage` draws the shared `StudioItemHeader`: a shield tile, the label, the api name chip, a Package chip (same `perm-provenance-badge` test id and the same three answers), "N objects granted · M field overrides", then Explain access (the pillar's button, opening the same panel), History as an outline chip, and a more button. The more menu holds "Edit name / label", which opens the name and label inputs that used to sit in the collapsible set header. The PageShell breadcrumb row, the badge row and the collapsible set header no longer render in Studio. The pillar draws its own header only for the OWD overview and the empty states.
- **Five tabs (target 3).** Objects (the landing), System capabilities, Row-level security, Tab visibility, Delegated admin. The pillar holds the tab (`accessTab`, default `objects`, kept across set switches) and passes it down. Every tab body stays mounted and the closed ones are `hidden`. This keeps the CEL lint of a row-level-security policy reporting to the autosave gate from any tab, and nothing typed is lost on a switch. `PermissionAdvancedFacets` gains an optional `only` prop that renders its three sections flat, one shown at a time.
- **Objects tab (target 4).** The toolbar has the object count, the filter, "Only granted" and the short legend with bold keys. Below it, a flush table: header row on the sidebar surface, 40 px rows, label plus mono api name, the OWD as a tinted chip (Private muted, public green, by parent blue; still `owd-badge-NAME` and still deep-linking to the overview), 18 px checkboxes with a 4 px radius, and dividers before C, before Tr and before the bulk column. The R · CRUD · All · None strip renders only on the hovered row or the row holding keyboard focus. Focus is read from real focus events (`onFocus` / `onBlur` with `relatedTarget`), not a class.
- **Rail (target 1).** Permission-set rows are 36 px, with the label on the first line and the api name in 10 px mono on the second. This is a `className` on the rows. `StudioRail.tsx` is not edited: the count and the add button were already there.
- **OWD overview header.** Its title and subtitle are now the pillar's item header (`engine.studio.owd.title` / `.subtitle`). The panel's own header row holds the description and Save (`owd-save` unchanged).

**Scope seam, as asked.** The Studio look is a NEW prop, `studio` (type `PermissionStudioChrome`), passed only by `AccessPillar` together with `embedded`. Setup's permission page (`builtinComponents.tsx`, no `studio`) renders exactly as before, so `embedded` keeps its meaning and its tests. `PermissionMatrixEditPage` is not re-exported from `@object-ui/app-shell`'s entry: `src/index.ts` names neither it nor `views/metadata-admin/index.js`, and `exports` has only `.` and `./styles.css`. The new prop is not a public-surface change.

**Write semantics are unchanged.** It is the same `updateObjectPerm` / `bulkSetObject` / `bulkSetFields`, the same autosave target and blocking conditions, the same four read-only gates, the destructive dialog and the clone flow. The shared JSX (notices, badges, basics inputs, capabilities, dialogs) was lifted into constants that both presentations render. The routed page's tree is the same.

**Merge with main.** objectui#12475 (`720f6d4`) gated History on `useCanReadAuthoringTrail`. That gate is kept in both presentations: the page's button and the Studio History chip both carry `data-testid="history-button"`, and the sheet renders only when the trail door admits the caller.

## Deviations from the artboard

1. **The draft / read-only note sits at the right end of the tab row**, not in the title row. At 1280 px the note ("This package's objects · read-only") in the title row truncated the label and the counts, which card acceptance 1 needs whole. It is the pillar's existing note, unchanged. objectui#12453 owns the read-only signals and lands next in this region.
2. **A chevron stays before each object label.** It opens the object's field-level R/W editor, the existing capability the artboard does not show.
3. **The Objects toolbar keeps the "Filter objects…" input**, and the count reads "M of N objects" while a filter narrows the list.
4. **A bulk-hint line sits under the matrix only when the set is writable**, as on the artboard. The artboard's second sentence ("Edits save as drafts…") is not repeated, because the header note says it.
5. **The OWD column header reads "OWD"** (a new key, `engine.studio.access.colOwd`), as on the artboard.
6. **The api-name chip shows in the header**, as on the artboard. No test on `main` pins the Access header's api name, and the Data pillar shows its chip the same way. objectui#7254 concerns the Interfaces surface.
7. **Checkboxes in a read-only package render disabled at 50 % opacity.** This is the existing read-only posture; objectui#12453 owns it. The screenshots are of hotcrm, which is a read-only code package.

## Tests (head `8327f04`, after merging origin/main `1c3b069`)

- New: `StudioDesignSurface.accessTabs-12456.test.tsx` (9 tests). It covers the header (label, api name, Package, "1 object granted · 0 field overrides", Explain / History / more), that the breadcrumb, badge row and band are gone, the five tabs in order with Objects the landing, each other tab showing its section, the facet tabs staying mounted, the bulk strip on hover only, the strip on keyboard focus and cleared when focus leaves the row, a bulk action writing what it wrote before, and the OWD chip and the count.
- Updated, same meaning: `StudioDesignSurface.accessGuard`, `StudioDesignSurface.pillarNavGuard` and `StudioDesignSurface.createAppOpensInterfaces-11794`. They hover the row before clicking its None button, and they read the open set's api name from the item header, because the mounted Delegated admin tab lists set names too.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on the 53 named and reached files (every `PermissionMatrixEditor*`, `AccessExplainPanel*`, `PackageOwdOverviewPanel*`, `StudioDesignSurface.access*`, `walledCatalogReadOnly-12183`, `packagedItemWriteGate-12169`, `trailDoorsGate-12475`, plus the guard tests above): 53 files, 358 tests passed, exit 0, on `8327f04`.
- Before the merge, on `11f3055`, all of `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` and `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/`: 666 files, 6928 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check`: exit 0 on `8327f04`. `build`: exit 0 on `11f3055`. `eslint` on the touched files: exit 0 (0 errors).
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys` exit 0 · `pnpm check:i18n-drift` exit 0 · `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0 · `pnpm check:new-line-citations` exit 0.
- Ablations, once each, through `ablation-replace.mjs` (each mutation landed, each run went red, and each file was restored to its HEAD blob):
  - accessGuard (the pillar's dirty confirm forced to pass): 4 failed.
  - accessRailLabels-11862 (rail secondary name dropped): 3 failed.
  - PackageOwdOverviewPanel (`owd-save` renamed): 4 failed across `.test` and `.layersUnsaved-11799`.
  - AccessExplainPanel (Explain button label changed): 5 failed.
  - accessTabs-12456 (strip always drawn): 2 failed.
  - accessTabs-12456 (landing tab changed to rls): 4 failed.
  - The first accessGuard attempt was refused by the tool as an ambiguous anchor and changed nothing. It was rerun with `--expect 2`.

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)

## Acceptance notes

- `PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx` is outside the claim's declared file surface. Three of the five tab bodies render there, so a tab-per-facet needs its sections to render one at a time. The edit is one additive optional prop (`only`); omitted, the stacked collapsibles render as before.
- The PM's mechanism assumptions, measured: (1) holds, apart from the parts this PR builds. (2) Partly holds: two of the five sections render in `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` and three in `PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx`. (3) The count and add button were already present, so no `StudioRail.tsx` edit was needed. (4) Done with focus events.
